ARVO metadata separately reports `7b3068c4bf7a217a1838db280072653197d30012` / `2fce6f81cc59144bf4f2f66f7620233d609b41ef` as the vulnerable/fixed commits. The staged worktree is an earlier equivalent RAR5 owner/group parser implementation carrying the same missing `>= OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` truncation obligation, and the staged `patch.diff` fixes that same logic in the later upstream revision.

classification.classification_note: The observed undefined behavior is an out-of-bounds stack-array index on the lvalue used for the trailing NUL write: the RAR5 owner parser fills `char namebuf[256]` and then computes `namebuf[256]` because the length clamp does not reserve space for the terminator.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 339-byte RAR5 witness drives libarchive through `rar5_read_header -> process_base_block -> process_head_file -> process_head_file_extra`, where the current FILE header carries an `EX_UOWNER` extra record. `parse_file_extra_owner()` decodes owner flags whose `OWNER_USER_NAME` bit is set, then reads an attacker-controlled user-name length and points `p` at that many owner bytes. In the vulnerable code, the user-name clamp treats only `value_len > OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` as oversized and otherwise leaves `name_len = value_len`; once the parsed length is 256 or larger, `name_len` becomes 256 even though `namebuf` is only `char namebuf[256]` and the code still appends a terminator after the copy. `memcpy(namebuf, p, name_len)` fills `namebuf[0..255]`, then `namebuf[name_len] = 0` computes `namebuf[256]` at line 1360. Stage 01 reproduced `UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: runtime error: index 256 out of bounds for type 'char [256]'` at that exact statement. The staged fix changes both owner-name branches to truncate `>= OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` down to `OWNER_MAXNAMELEN - 1` before the terminator write.

source.description: First project-code read inside the crashing owner-extra parser that materializes attacker-controlled state used by the vulnerability path.
source.value_from: Stage 01 reproduced the crash on the exact staged 339-byte RAR5 witness. On that path, `process_head_file_extra()` dispatches `EX_UOWNER` to this parser at line 1441, and the later crash at line 1360 proves that the decoded flags include `OWNER_USER_NAME` and therefore route execution into the first owner-name branch.
source.note: This read decodes the owner-field flags varint. Because the saved UBSan crash lands in the first owner-name branch at line 1360, the resulting `flags` state necessarily satisfies `(flags & OWNER_USER_NAME) != 0` on the witnessed path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: UBSan crash site. The parser appends a NUL terminator using out-of-bounds subscript `namebuf[256]` on the fixed 256-byte stack buffer.
sink.note: The saved UBSan trace reports `runtime error: index 256 out of bounds for type 'char [256]'` at `parse_file_extra_owner:1360:21`, and Stage 01's reproduction summary names the same file, function, and line.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The user-name clamp allows `name_len` to become 256 instead of reserving one byte for the trailing NUL.
root_cause.note: On the crashing path, the parsed user-name length is large enough that this code leaves `name_len == OWNER_MAXNAMELEN`. The later terminator store at line 1360 therefore targets index 256 of `namebuf[256]`. The staged patch fixes the exact obligation by changing the threshold to `>= OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` and truncating to `OWNER_MAXNAMELEN - 1` before the terminator write.

parser_admitted.description: On the saved crashing path, the current RAR5 FILE extra-field ID decodes as `EX_UOWNER`, so `process_head_file_extra()` enters `parse_file_extra_owner()`. The surrounding stack frames at `process_head_file:1618` and `process_base_block:1924` show that this happens while parsing a RAR5 file header's extra data.

tainted_value_origin.description: This read materializes the attacker-controlled user-name length that later becomes both the copy size and the terminator index.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the crashing path, this is the length field of the `OWNER_USER_NAME` payload inside the `EX_UOWNER` extra record. The later out-of-bounds subscript proves that it decodes to a value that makes the vulnerable clamp leave `name_len == OWNER_MAXNAMELEN`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The owner parser decodes the attacker-controlled flags field. Because the saved crash is the user-name terminator expression at line 1360, this decoded state makes `(flags & OWNER_USER_NAME) != 0` and therefore selects the first owner-name branch.
Inside the user-name arm, the parser reads the attacker-controlled user-name length and obtains `p`, a pointer to that many owner-name bytes. Steps 3 and 4 use this exact length and source buffer.

Root cause. This clamp treats only `value_len > 256` as oversized and otherwise preserves the parsed length. On the witnessed crashing path, the parsed user-name length is large enough that this code leaves `name_len == 256`, so the later terminator subscript has no in-bounds slot left in `char namebuf[256]`.

The copy uses the attacker-controlled bytes at `p` and the unclamped `name_len` from step 3. With `name_len == 256`, it fills every valid byte of `namebuf[0..255]` and leaves no room for a trailing NUL.

Sink. The parser appends the terminator using the same `name_len` computed in step 3. Because step 4 already filled the 256-byte destination, this lvalue subscript computes `namebuf[256]`, matching the saved UBSan `index 256 out of bounds for type 'char [256]'` at line 1360.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes. The staged `patch.diff` changes both owner-name branches in `parse_file_extra_owner()` from allowing `name_len = OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` to truncating `>= OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` down to `OWNER_MAXNAMELEN - 1` before the terminator write, which is exactly the missing guard on the crashing user-name path.

poc.trigger: Feeding the staged 339-byte `poc` RAR5 archive to the vulnerable Stage 01 `libarchive_fuzzer` reproduces the saved `UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: index 256 out of bounds for type 'char [256]'` report in `parse_file_extra_owner()`.

format.name: 339-byte RAR5 file header carrying an owner extra record with an oversized user name
format.contract: The witness is a raw RAR5 archive beginning with the standard signature `52 61 72 21 1a 07 01 00`. On the crashing header, `process_base_block()` dispatches a `HEAD_FILE` block to `process_head_file()`, `process_head_file_extra()` decodes the current extra-field ID as `EX_UOWNER`, and `parse_file_extra_owner()` takes the `OWNER_USER_NAME` branch. The trigger condition is an owner user-name length varint that decodes to at least `OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` (256) with that many bytes available, so the vulnerable clamp leaves `name_len == 256`, `memcpy()` fills `namebuf[0..255]`, and the subsequent terminator expression computes `namebuf[name_len]` at index 256, matching the staged UBSan report at line 1360.
